endorsements.quote: Equity safeguards: require subgroup performance reporting and representativeness audits for every AI-enabled RWE submission.
Dataset representativeness: Evidence that training data cover relevant age, sex, ethnicity, and comorbidity distributions.
Human-factors testing: Usability testing with clinicians and patients to assess workflow fit and risk of alert fatigue.
This checklist can also serve as a procurement and payer assessment tool, ensuring that AI solutions adopted into healthcare contracts meet equity and fairness standards.
We propose systematic triggers for retraining when calibration deteriorates, ensuring that predictive tools remain safe and equitable across diverse sites ( 18 , 45 , 61 ).
Model explainability: Availability of explanations appropriate for clinicians (e.g., SHAP plots, feature importance).
Clinicians and health systems: adopt site-readiness criteria; train staff to integrate ePROs, PGHD, and AI decision-support tools into workflows.

We propose a short checklist: (1) audit demographic representativeness of training data; (2) report subgroup performance metrics; (3) apply fairness indicators (e.g., calibration by sex, ethnicity, age); and (4) disclose limitations openly.

unlisted_practices: Regulators should require regulatory-grade AI validation frameworks ensuring external validation, subgroup performance reporting, and post-deployment monitoring.
Establish harmonized privacy-by-design governance for IoT and continuous lifestyle and environmental data streams, ensuring they are securely managed, consented, and interoperable.
Adopt dynamic consent and improved data custodianship for patient data used in predictive tools.
Give patients clear, honest explanations of AI predictions informing their care, decisions made on their behalf, and how their data are used.
Involve patients and the public early and throughout in the development and governance of AI-enabled care, including participation in governance boards.
Payers should include remote monitoring and AI-enabled diagnostics in reimbursement pilots and define reimbursable endpoints beyond drug efficacy.
Industry should publish protocols and validation datasets for AI models and establish equity dashboards.
Health systems should invest in digital capacity and workforce, particularly in underserved and rural communities, to implement AI equitably.
Health systems should provide staff training modules for AI-supported decision-making.
Use common data models such as OMOP and interoperability standards such as FHIR and DICOM for RWE-based AI.
Prespecify and publicly register study protocols and report deviations for RWE studies, including publication of negative findings.
Maintain an end-to-end audit trail linking raw real-world data to the final analysis dataset.

screen.reason: This review/perspective paper provides frameworks and actionable checklists (pre-deployment audit, equity checklist, regulatory pragmatics) for deploying and governing AI and real-world evidence in personalized medicine.
